svg.title: Credit-to-Cash Conversion Costs
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-credit-to-cash-cost-ranges; chapter number: 2; title: Credit-to-Cash Conversion Costs; subtitle: Liquidators, invoice routes and balance-transfer checks compared; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: percent of amount converted; bars: label: Credit card liquidator fee; min: 5; max: 6; typical: 5.5; display: 5% to 6% (Alex Barajas); label: Balance-transfer checks; min: 3; max: 5; typical: 4; display: 3% to 5%; label: Net liquidation cost after rewards; min: 4; max: 4; typical: 4; display: About 4% (Naam Wynn); label: Invoice and PayPal routes; min: 2; max: 3; typical: 2.5; display: About 2% to 3%; label: Card rewards netted back; min: 2; max: 2; typical: 2; display: 2% card rewards (Naam Wynn); caption: Credit converted to cash only pays when a buyer, exit or repayment plan is locked before the swipe; Naam Wynn nets 2% rewards against a 6%+ liquidator fee for a real cost near 4%.; assumptions note: Typical marks the midpoint where only a range was quoted. Send $100 through any route and confirm it lands before moving thousands; 1099-K reporting threshold was $5,000 for 2024 (James Baker CPA).; note: Sources - Alex Barajas, Naam Wynn, Geobreeze Travel, James Baker CPA, Frequent Miler.
